title: Stackline — Parametric Object Lab
summary: An original offline desk-organizer configurator with three parameterized two-part designs, six checked closed-manifold STL solids, dimensioned SVG drawings, BOMs, local ZIP downloads, modeled material/cost/assembly comparisons, and explicit unperformed physical inspection gates. Includes a Pocket Arcade card/token extension and a held 196 mm packing-change review.
limitations: Digital manufacturing-review work only. No fabrication, orders, material selection, machine operation, physical measurements, shipment, publication, spending, services or native Hive setup occurred.
STL coordinates are nominal mm, but STL has no unit metadata: import explicitly at 1:1 mm. No slicer, CAD import, infill, support, shrinkage, process or print-behavior validation is claimed.

Clearance, wall/rib limits and inspection tolerances are design/review assumptions, not validated process capability or strength. The loose insert is unretained and its bays do not seal small objects.
All mass, feedstock, cost, effort, packaging and five inspection fixture rows are synthetic/modeled. Assembly effort includes handling/inspection and is not a time study or fabrication-time estimate.
Pocket Arcade is an original card/token concept using assumed payload dimensions; actual game-item fit, retention, retrieval, stability and durability are untested.
The proposed 196 mm design is HOLD against the current fixed packing envelope. Baseline samples do not validate a width change or any real batch.
Physical prototype approval, material/process safety and suitability, dimensional and fit trials, surface/stability/strength review, real handling time and transit protection remain unperformed.
Real-browser visual and accessibility review is parent-owned and not claimed by this workstream; app behavior was checked with an original minimal DOM harness.
Only lightweight dry desk use is in scope; food, heated items, electrical, medical, child-safety and load-bearing uses are excluded.
